imageCompressor.title: Compress image files without uploading
imageCompressor.paragraph1: Use this image compressor when a JPG, PNG, or WebP file is too large for email, forms, websites, or chat apps.
imageCompressor.paragraph2: The compression runs in your browser, so selected images stay on your device while you choose quality and download smaller files.
imageCompressor.useCase1: Reduce product photos before uploading them to a store or CMS.
imageCompressor.useCase2: Make screenshots and phone photos small enough for email attachments.
imageCompressor.useCase3: Shrink blog, profile, and document images while keeping a practical preview quality.
imageCompressor.step1: Choose JPG, PNG, or WebP images.
imageCompressor.step2: Adjust the quality and output format.
imageCompressor.step3: Process the files and download the compressed results.
imageCompressor.faq1Question: Which image formats can I compress?
imageCompressor.faq1Answer: You can compress JPG, PNG, and WebP images.
imageCompressor.faq2Question: Will compression change the image dimensions?
imageCompressor.faq2Answer: No. This tool reduces file size with quality settings and keeps the original dimensions.

imageConverter.title: Convert JPG, PNG, and WebP online
imageConverter.paragraph1: Use this image converter to change image formats for websites, documents, social posts, and browser compatibility.
imageConverter.paragraph2: Conversion happens locally in your browser, so the original image does not need to be uploaded before you download the new file.
imageConverter.useCase1: Convert PNG screenshots to smaller JPG files.
imageConverter.useCase2: Create WebP images for modern web pages.
imageConverter.useCase3: Turn WebP downloads into JPG or PNG for older apps.
imageConverter.step1: Choose one or more supported images.
imageConverter.step2: Pick JPG, PNG, WebP, or keep the same format.
imageConverter.step3: Convert and download the new image files.
imageConverter.faq1Question: Can I convert multiple images at once?
imageConverter.faq1Answer: Yes. You can select several JPG, PNG, or WebP images and convert them together.
imageConverter.faq2Answer: No. The conversion is handled directly in your browser.

imageToPdf.title: Create a PDF from images
imageToPdf.paragraph1: Use this image to PDF converter when you need to turn photos, scans, screenshots, or design exports into one PDF file.
imageToPdf.paragraph2: You can sort images before creating the PDF, then download the finished document from your browser.
imageToPdf.useCase1: Combine scanned receipts, forms, or notes into one PDF.
imageToPdf.useCase2: Send multiple screenshots as a single document.
imageToPdf.useCase3: Create a simple PDF from JPG, PNG, or WebP images.
imageToPdf.step1: Choose the images you want in the PDF.
imageToPdf.step2: Adjust order, page size, orientation, margin, and background.
imageToPdf.faq1Question: Can I change the image order?
imageToPdf.faq1Answer: Yes. Move files up or down before creating the PDF.
imageToPdf.faq2Answer: JPG, PNG, and WebP images are supported.

cropImage.title: Crop images for avatars, covers, and uploads
cropImage.paragraph1: Use this image cropper to remove extra space and prepare a cleaner image for profiles, documents, and web pages.
cropImage.paragraph2: The preview and crop settings run in your browser, so you can adjust the visible area before downloading.
cropImage.useCase1: Crop profile pictures to a square.
cropImage.useCase2: Prepare cover images with common ratios.
cropImage.useCase3: Remove unwanted edges from screenshots or scans.
cropImage.step1: Choose one JPG, PNG, or WebP image.
cropImage.step2: Pick a crop ratio and adjust the crop area.
cropImage.faq1Question: Can I crop with a fixed ratio?
cropImage.faq1Answer: Yes. The tool includes free, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, and 3:4 ratios.
cropImage.faq2Question: Is the image uploaded while cropping?
cropImage.faq2Answer: No. Cropping is handled in your browser.

rotateImage.title: Rotate and flip images in the browser
rotateImage.paragraph1: Use this image rotation tool to fix sideways phone photos, scanned pages, screenshots, and images saved in the wrong direction.
rotateImage.paragraph2: Each selected image can have its own rotation or flip setting before you download the corrected result.
rotateImage.useCase1: Fix phone photos that open sideways.
rotateImage.useCase2: Rotate scanned pages before sending them.
rotateImage.useCase3: Flip images horizontally or vertically for layout needs.
rotateImage.step2: Set rotate or flip options for each file.
rotateImage.step3: Process and download the corrected images.
rotateImage.faq1Question: Can each image use different rotation settings?
rotateImage.faq1Answer: Yes. Rotation controls are shown per selected image.
rotateImage.faq2Answer: You can keep the original format or export JPG, PNG, or WebP.

mergePdf.title: Merge PDF files into one document
mergePdf.paragraph1: Use this PDF merger when several PDFs need to become one file for email, archiving, upload forms, or document delivery.
mergePdf.paragraph2: You can choose multiple PDFs, set their order, and create one combined PDF directly in your browser.
mergePdf.useCase1: Combine invoices, reports, or forms into one file.
mergePdf.useCase2: Merge scanned PDF parts before uploading.
mergePdf.useCase3: Create one document from separate PDF chapters or attachments.
mergePdf.step1: Choose at least two PDF files.
mergePdf.step3: Merge and download the combined PDF.
mergePdf.faq1Question: Can I reorder PDFs before merging?
mergePdf.faq1Answer: Yes. Move files up or down to control the final order.
mergePdf.faq2Answer: No. Supported merging runs in your browser.

splitPdf.title: Extract selected pages from a PDF
splitPdf.paragraph1: Use this PDF splitter when you only need certain pages from a longer PDF document.
splitPdf.paragraph2: Enter a page range such as all, 1-3, or 1,4,8, then export the selected pages as a new PDF.
splitPdf.useCase1: Send only the pages someone needs.
splitPdf.useCase2: Extract a form, receipt, or chapter from a larger PDF.
splitPdf.step2: Enter the page range you want to keep.
splitPdf.step3: Split and download the new PDF.
splitPdf.faq1Question: What page range format can I use?
splitPdf.faq1Answer: Use all, a range like 1-3, or individual pages like 1,4,8.
splitPdf.faq2Question: Does splitting edit the original file?
splitPdf.faq2Answer: No. The original PDF stays unchanged on your device.

compressPdf.title: Compress PDF files for upload and email
compressPdf.paragraph1: Use this PDF compressor when a PDF is too large for email attachments, form uploads, or document portals.
compressPdf.paragraph2: Compression depends on the PDF content. Some PDFs are already optimized, while image-heavy PDFs usually have more room to shrink.
compressPdf.useCase1: Reduce PDF attachments before sending email.
compressPdf.useCase2: Make scanned PDFs smaller for upload limits.
compressPdf.useCase3: Try browser-based PDF compression before installing software.
compressPdf.faq1Question: Why did my PDF not get smaller?
compressPdf.faq1Answer: Some PDFs are already compressed or contain content that cannot be reduced much in the browser.
compressPdf.faq2Answer: Some stronger compression modes may rasterize pages, so text may no longer be selectable.

pdfToImages.title: Convert PDF pages to images
pdfToImages.paragraph1: Use this PDF to images converter to export PDF pages as JPG or PNG files for previews, sharing, slides, or documents.
pdfToImages.paragraph2: Pages are rendered in order in your browser, then you can download the image results.
pdfToImages.useCase1: Create image previews from PDF pages.
pdfToImages.useCase2: Save a PDF page as a JPG or PNG for sharing.
pdfToImages.useCase3: Insert PDF pages into documents or presentations as images.
pdfToImages.faq1Answer: Yes. The tool exports PDF pages in order.
pdfToImages.faq2Question: Are page images generated on the server?
pdfToImages.faq2Answer: No. Supported rendering happens in your browser.

resizeImage.title: Resize images by width or height
resizeImage.paragraph1: Use this image resizer when an image needs exact dimensions for web pages, email, forms, or documents.
resizeImage.paragraph2: You can keep the original aspect ratio so images do not look stretched after resizing.
resizeImage.useCase1: Prepare images for website upload requirements.
resizeImage.useCase2: Resize photos before sending them by email.
resizeImage.useCase3: Create smaller dimensions for documents or previews.
resizeImage.step1: Choose JPG, PNG, or WebP images.
resizeImage.step2: Enter the target width or height.
resizeImage.step3: Resize and download the output files.
resizeImage.faq1Question: Can the tool keep the aspect ratio?
resizeImage.faq1Answer: Yes. Keep aspect ratio is available to avoid stretching images.
resizeImage.faq2Answer: Yes. Multiple images can be resized together.

qrCode.title: Create QR codes from text, links, or images
qrCode.paragraph1: Use this QR code generator to create a downloadable PNG QR code for links, short text, contact details, or small image payloads.
qrCode.paragraph2: The QR code is generated in your browser, so the content does not need to be sent to this server.
qrCode.useCase1: Create QR codes for websites, menus, posters, or documents.
qrCode.useCase2: Turn short text or contact information into a scannable code.
qrCode.useCase3: Download a PNG QR code for printing or sharing.
qrCode.step1: Enter text, paste a link, or choose an image.
qrCode.step2: Adjust size, colors, and quiet zone.
qrCode.step3: Generate and download the PNG QR code.
qrCode.faq1Question: Can I customize QR code colors?
qrCode.faq1Answer: Yes. You can set foreground and background colors.
qrCode.faq2Question: Why can an image QR code fail?
qrCode.faq2Answer: A QR code can only hold limited data, so large or complex images may be too big.
